outcome.technical: run-test-gate.py: the red-first stage now runs in a thread beside the gate's steps (`_run_beside`), the per-step body moved verbatim into `_gate_step` so both threads read a step by the same rules; `_shell` takes an optional `stop` event (`_communicate` polls every STOP_POLL_SECONDS) and tears the group down on it, the step carrying TORN_DOWN; only the default runner is made stoppable (`_stopping`), and only when a stage exists. A stage red sets the gate's stop: the step in flight is torn down, no later one starts, and every gate step is recorded not run, stoppedBy the first red stage step, under RED_FIRST_NOT_RUN or RED_FIRST_SET_ASIDE (a step that answered first; its exit named, its followers kept); both sentences name the stage first so the row's basis bound keeps it. A torn-down step makes the tree comparison a race, said in treeBasis. New `red_first_beside(stage, commands, manifest, phase_id)` takes the stage's suites out of every gate step that is the recorded spelling over a path list still holding another path, returns the stage names leaned on (`held`) and one line per narrowed or keeping step; main passes the narrowed commands and `red_first_held` to run_gate, prints the lines, and publishes a narrowed declared command (`_narrowed_published`). A green stage named in red_first_held stays a step of the row at its head; one not named leaves as before (redFirstStage). _evidence_io.py: RED_FIRST_STEP_PREFIX comment and declared_steps docstring updated (no code change). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: run-test-gate's red-first paragraph rewritten. changelog.d/P173.8.changed.md added (release.py changelog-check exit 0). Tests: tests/test_run_test_gate.py new block rfb (rfb1-rfb6) plus `_ps_repo(joined=True)` fixture; rf1/rf3/rf6/rf7/rfu1/rfu2 now compare calls as a multiset / one stage call (order is the scheduler's beside the gate); tests/test__evidence_io.py pgs3 locks declared_steps over a leaned-on stage step (regression lock, passes on base too). One assertion of my own drafted rfb1 was corrected after the first green run: I had expected declared_steps to return the joined name, it returns the declared entry head (as jn4/jst3 pin) - the plan's gate. Commands: gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_run_test_gate.py tests/test__evidence_io.py` exit 0 (2/2 files ok, 1417 cases; test_run_test_gate 805 cases); pre-gate `python3 tools/lints/_deps.py --register-citations` exit 0; ruff exit 0; vermin -t=3.8- exit 0; extra: sweep of tests/test__proc_group.py tests/test__output_lints.py tests/test__deps.py exit 0 (3/3 files ok). Mutation probes in a scratch copy (scratchpad/mut/probe.py): no narrowing -> rfb1,rfb4 red; held never -> rfb1,rfb4 red; held always -> rf3,rfb5 red; stage joined before gate (serial) -> rfb2,rfb3,rfb6 red; stop ignored by _shell -> rfb3 red. Dependants: drive-phase.py and full-gate.py run run-test-gate.py as a subprocess - still correct: the step order on a stopped row is unchanged ([stage..., gate...], gate steps not run with stoppedBy) and the new printed lines open with the existing `[run-test-gate] red-first:` prefix; gate_red_decision/red_runs read runId and failing lines, not step positions. commit-task-work.py verdict and _verdict_binding read the declared gate through declared_steps, which reads past leading red-first steps (pgs3, rf2b) - unchanged. last_task_row unchanged; a green row with a leading green stage step is not red, so it starts no stage next round. _evidence_io._counts_as_failed: a not-run step has exit None and a green stage step exit 0, neither counts. Coverage: a held stage's output joins the row's texts, so the suite it ran is covered; a non-held green stage's output still leaves (rfu4-rfu6 green). test__proc_group (GATE._shell positional calls) still correct, stop defaults to None - suite green. test__panel_composition, test_audit_lookup, test_commit_task_work, test_derive_phase_gate, test_drive_phase, test_drive_without_model import or reference run-test-gate: not run here (outside own-tests; test_drive_phase is the expensive suite) - they call no renamed name: no public name was removed or renamed; run_gate gained a keyword (red_first_held) and _shell a keyword (stop). outcome.descriptive: A re-gate after a one-suite red now runs that suite once, beside the rest of the gate, instead of alone first and then again inside the gate.

testsAdded: rfb1: a re-gate after a one-suite red over a joined step hands the runner that suite once (the stage) and the joined step without it, green, stage kept at the head of the row
rfb2: the stage's command and the gate's step each see the other started (they overlap)
rfb3: a red stage tears down the gate step in flight (started marker, no done marker, well under its sleep) and records it not run, stopped by the stage
rfb4: red_first_beside narrows a wider spelled step, keeps the suite in a step over it alone and in the bare step (one line each), leaves an unrelated step unsaid
rfb5: a stage whose suite no step lists takes nothing out and holds nothing
rfb6: a gate step that answered before the stage's red is recorded not run, its answer set aside, basis naming the stage and the exit
pgs3 (test__evidence_io): declared_steps reads past a leading green red-first step a gate step leaned on
